<STRUCT_0001>
Rigidification is a process for removing a flat subgroup from the inertia.
For example, if <MATH_0001> is a projective variety, the morphism from the Picard
stack to the Picard scheme is a rigidification of the group of automorphism
<MATH_0002>.

<STRUCT_0006> Romagny: <EMPHOPEN_0002>Group actions on stacks and applications<EMPHCLOSE_0002>
<REF_0002>
<STRUCT_0007>

<STRUCT_0009> Abramovich, Graber, Vistoli:
<EMPHOPEN_0003>Gromov-Witten theory for Deligne-Mumford stacks<EMPHCLOSE_0003> <REF_0003>
<STRUCT_0010>
The appendix gives a summary of rigidification as in <REF_0004> with two
alternative interpretations. This paper also contains constructions for
gluing algebraic stacks along closed substacks and for taking roots of line
bundles.
